## I APPLICATION OF THIS PART

## Scope and interpretation

## 82.1

[PART 82 – CLOSED MATERIAL PROCEDURE > 82.1] (1) This Part contains rules—

[PART 82 – CLOSED MATERIAL PROCEDURE > 82.1] (a) about—

[PART 82 – CLOSED MATERIAL PROCEDURE > 82.1] (i) applications under sections 6(2), 7(4) and 18(1) of the Justice and Security Act 2013;

[PART 82 – CLOSED MATERIAL PROCEDURE > 82.1] (ii) closed material applications in section 6 proceedings;

[PART 82 – CLOSED MATERIAL PROCEDURE > 82.1] (iii) section 6 proceedings; and

[PART 82 – CLOSED MATERIAL PROCEDURE > 82.1] (b) about appeals to the Court of Appeal where there have been proceedings on or in relation to any matter within sub-paragraph (a) in the High Court. [PART 82 – CLOSED MATERIAL PROCEDURE > 82.1] (2) Subject to paragraph (3), in this Part—

[PART 82 – CLOSED MATERIAL PROCEDURE > 82.1] (a) ‘the Act’ means the Justice and Security Act 2013;

[PART 82 – CLOSED MATERIAL PROCEDURE > 82.1] (b) ‘closed material application’ means an application of the kind mentioned in section 8(1)(a) of the Act;

[PART 82 – CLOSED MATERIAL PROCEDURE > 82.1] (c) ‘legal representative’ is to be construed in accordance with section 14(1) of the Act;

[PART 82 – CLOSED MATERIAL PROCEDURE > 82.1] (d) ‘relevant person’ is to be construed in accordance with section 14(1) of the Act;

[PART 82 – CLOSED MATERIAL PROCEDURE > 82.1] (e) ‘section 6 proceedings’ is to be construed in accordance with section 14(1) of the Act;

[PART 82 – CLOSED MATERIAL PROCEDURE > 82.1] (f) ‘sensitive material’ has the meaning given by section 6(11) of the Act;

[PART 82 – CLOSED MATERIAL PROCEDURE > 82.1] (g) ‘special advocate’ means a person appointed under section 9(1) of the Act;

[PART 82 – CLOSED MATERIAL PROCEDURE > 82.1] (h) ‘specially represented party’ means a party whose interests a special advocate represents;

[PART 82 – CLOSED MATERIAL PROCEDURE > 82.1] (3) In relation to proceedings arising by virtue of section 18 of the Act (review of certification)—

[PART 82 – CLOSED MATERIAL PROCEDURE > 82.1] (a) a reference to the relevant person is to be read as a reference to the Secretary of State; and

[PART 82 – CLOSED MATERIAL PROCEDURE > 82.1] (b) a reference to the interests of national security includes a reference to the interests of the international relations of the United Kingdom. ## Modification to the overriding objective

## 82.2

[PART 82 – CLOSED MATERIAL PROCEDURE > 82.2] (1) Where any of the rules in this Part applies, the overriding objective in Part 1, and so far as possible any other rule, must be read and given effect in a way which is compatible with the duty set out in paragraph (2). [PART 82 – CLOSED MATERIAL PROCEDURE > 82.2] (2) The court must ensure that information is not disclosed in a way which would be damaging to the interests of national security. [PART 82 – CLOSED MATERIAL PROCEDURE > 82.2] (3) Subject to paragraph (2), the court must satisfy itself that the material available to it enables it properly to determine proceedings. ## Rules to apply subject to this Part

## 82.3

[PART 82 – CLOSED MATERIAL PROCEDURE > 82.3] (1) Subject to paragraph (2), in relation to proceedings to which this Part applies, these Rules apply subject to the rules in this Part. [PART 82 – CLOSED MATERIAL PROCEDURE > 82.3] (2) Part 31 (disclosure and inspection of documents) applies to proceedings to which this Part applies, subject only to rule 82.2 and the court’s permission for material not to be disclosed otherwise than to—

[PART 82 – CLOSED MATERIAL PROCEDURE > 82.3] (a) the court;

[PART 82 – CLOSED MATERIAL PROCEDURE > 82.3] (b) any person appointed as a special advocate; and

[PART 82 – CLOSED MATERIAL PROCEDURE > 82.3] (c) where the Secretary of State is not the relevant person but is a party to the proceedings, the Secretary of State. ## II GENERAL PROVISIONS

## Scope of this section

[PART 82 – CLOSED MATERIAL PROCEDURE > Scope of this section] 82.4 This section applies, except where otherwise indicated, to the proceedings mentioned in rule 82.1. ## Case management

## 82.5

[PART 82 – CLOSED MATERIAL PROCEDURE > 82.5] (1) Proceedings to which this Section applies are to be treated as allocated (or, as the case may be, re-allocated) to the multi-track. [PART 82 – CLOSED MATERIAL PROCEDURE > 82.5] (2) Subject to paragraph (3), Section II of Part 3 does not apply to proceedings in which a declaration has been made under section 6(2) of the Act. [PART 82 – CLOSED MATERIAL PROCEDURE > 82.5] (3) When a declaration is made under section 6(2) of the Act—

[PART 82 – CLOSED MATERIAL PROCEDURE > 82.5] (a) a costs management order that has already been made shall not apply to any costs incurred after the declaration is made; and

[PART 82 – CLOSED MATERIAL PROCEDURE > 82.5] (b) the court may make any other order in relation to costs incurred before the declaration is made that it considers appropriate. ## Hearings in private

## 82.6

[PART 82 – CLOSED MATERIAL PROCEDURE > 82.6] (1) If the court considers it necessary for any party and that party’s legal representative to be excluded from any hearing or part of a hearing in order to secure that information is not disclosed where disclosure would be damaging to the interests of national security, it must—

[PART 82 – CLOSED MATERIAL PROCEDURE > 82.6] (a) direct accordingly; and

[PART 82 – CLOSED MATERIAL PROCEDURE > 82.6] (b) conduct the hearing, or that part of it from which that party and that party’s legal representative are excluded, in private but attended by a special advocate to represent the interests of the excluded party. [PART 82 – CLOSED MATERIAL PROCEDURE > 82.6] (2) The court may conduct a hearing or part of a hearing in private for any other good reason. ## Notification of hearings

[PART 82 – CLOSED MATERIAL PROCEDURE > Notification of hearings] 82.7 Unless the court directs otherwise, it must serve notice of the date, time and place fixed for any hearing on—

[PART 82 – CLOSED MATERIAL PROCEDURE > Notification of hearings] (a) every party, whether or not entitled to attend that hearing; and

[PART 82 – CLOSED MATERIAL PROCEDURE > Notification of hearings] (b) the special advocate or those instructing the special advocate. ## Proceedings which must be determined at a hearing

[PART 82 – CLOSED MATERIAL PROCEDURE > Proceedings which must be determined at a hearing] 82.8 The following proceedings must, unless the court directs otherwise, be determined at a hearing—

[PART 82 – CLOSED MATERIAL PROCEDURE > Proceedings which must be determined at a hearing] (a) an application by the Secretary of State under section 6(2) of the Act for a declaration;

[PART 82 – CLOSED MATERIAL PROCEDURE > Proceedings which must be determined at a hearing] (b) a closed material application;

[PART 82 – CLOSED MATERIAL PROCEDURE > Proceedings which must be determined at a hearing] (c) a review of the court’s own motion under section 7 of a declaration made under section 6 of the Act;

[PART 82 – CLOSED MATERIAL PROCEDURE > Proceedings which must be determined at a hearing] (d) a formal review under section 7(3) of the Act of a declaration made under section 6 of the Act;

[PART 82 – CLOSED MATERIAL PROCEDURE > Proceedings which must be determined at a hearing] (e) an application under section 7 of the Act for revocation of a declaration made under section 6 of the Act;

[PART 82 – CLOSED MATERIAL PROCEDURE > Proceedings which must be determined at a hearing] (f) an application under section 18(1) of the Act to have a certificate issued under section 17(3)(e) of the Act set aside;

[PART 82 – CLOSED MATERIAL PROCEDURE > Proceedings which must be determined at a hearing] (g) an appeal to the Court of Appeal from a decision or order of the High Court made in any of the proceedings mentioned in paragraphs (a) to (f) above. ## Appointment of a special advocate

## 82.9

[PART 82 – CLOSED MATERIAL PROCEDURE > 82.9] (1) Subject to paragraphs (2) and (3), where—

[PART 82 – CLOSED MATERIAL PROCEDURE > 82.9] (a) the Secretary of State decides to make an application under section 6(2) of the Act for a declaration; or

[PART 82 – CLOSED MATERIAL PROCEDURE > 82.9] (b) the Secretary of State receives written notice under rule 82.21 (notification of intention to make application for a declaration) that a party other than the Secretary of State intends to make such an application; or

[PART 82 – CLOSED MATERIAL PROCEDURE > 82.9] (c) the Secretary of State receives written notice under rule 82.31 (review of certification) of an application under section 18(1) of the Act to have a certificate issued under section 17(3)(e) of the Act set aside, the Secretary of State must immediately give notice of the proceedings to the Attorney General (who, under section 9(1) of the Act, has the power to appoint a special advocate). [PART 82 – CLOSED MATERIAL PROCEDURE > 82.9] (2) Paragraph (1) applies unless a special advocate has already been appointed to represent the interests of the specially represented party in the proceedings and that special advocate is not prevented from communicating with that party by virtue of rule 82.11 (special advocate: communicating about proceedings). [PART 82 – CLOSED MATERIAL PROCEDURE > 82.9] (3) Paragraph (1) applies whether the proceedings are in the High Court or the Court of Appeal. [PART 82 – CLOSED MATERIAL PROCEDURE > 82.9] (4) Where any proceedings to which this Section applies are pending but no special advocate has been appointed, any party or the Secretary of State may request that the Attorney General appoint a special advocate. ## Functions of a special advocate

[PART 82 – CLOSED MATERIAL PROCEDURE > Functions of a special advocate] 82.10 The functions of a special advocate are to represent the interests of a specially represented party by—

[PART 82 – CLOSED MATERIAL PROCEDURE > Functions of a special advocate] (a) making submissions to the court at any hearing or part of a hearing from which the specially represented party and the specially represented party’s legal representatives are excluded;

[PART 82 – CLOSED MATERIAL PROCEDURE > Functions of a special advocate] (b) adducing evidence and cross-examining witnesses at any such hearing or part of a hearing;

[PART 82 – CLOSED MATERIAL PROCEDURE > Functions of a special advocate] (c) making applications to the court or seeking directions from the court where necessary; and

[PART 82 – CLOSED MATERIAL PROCEDURE > Functions of a special advocate] (d) making written submissions to the court. ## Special advocate: communicating about proceedings

## 82.11

[PART 82 – CLOSED MATERIAL PROCEDURE > 82.11] (1) The special advocate may communicate with the specially represented party or the specially represented party’s legal representative at any time before a relevant person serves sensitive material on the special advocate. [PART 82 – CLOSED MATERIAL PROCEDURE > 82.11] (2) After the relevant person serves sensitive material on the special advocate, the special advocate must not communicate with any person about any matter connected with the proceedings, except in accordance with paragraph (3), (3A) or (6)(b) or with a direction of the court pursuant to a request under paragraph (4). [PART 82 – CLOSED MATERIAL PROCEDURE > 82.11] (3) The special advocate may, without directions from the court, communicate about the proceedings with—

[PART 82 – CLOSED MATERIAL PROCEDURE > 82.11] (a) the court;

[PART 82 – CLOSED MATERIAL PROCEDURE > 82.11] (b) the relevant person (where this is not the Secretary of State);

[PART 82 – CLOSED MATERIAL PROCEDURE > 82.11] (c) the Secretary of State or any person acting for the Secretary of State;

[PART 82 – CLOSED MATERIAL PROCEDURE > 82.11] (d) the Attorney General or any person acting for the Attorney General; or

[PART 82 – CLOSED MATERIAL PROCEDURE > 82.11] (e) any other person, except the specially represented party or the specially represented party’s legal representative, with whom it is necessary for administrative purposes for the special advocate to communicate about matters not connected with the substance of the proceedings. [PART 82 – CLOSED MATERIAL PROCEDURE > 82.11] (3A) The special advocate may communicate with the specially represented party or the specially represented party’s legal representative with the express agreement of the relevant person and (where the relevant person is not the Secretary of State) the Secretary of State. [PART 82 – CLOSED MATERIAL PROCEDURE > 82.11] (4) The special advocate may request directions from the court authorising the special advocate to communicate with the specially represented party or the specially represented party’s legal representative or with any other person. [PART 82 – CLOSED MATERIAL PROCEDURE > 82.11] (5) Where the special advocate makes a request for directions under paragraph (4)—

[PART 82 – CLOSED MATERIAL PROCEDURE > 82.11] (a) the court must notify the relevant person, and (where the relevant person is not the Secretary of State) the Secretary of State, of the request and of the content of the proposed communication and the form in which it is proposed to be made; and

[PART 82 – CLOSED MATERIAL PROCEDURE > 82.11] (b) the relevant person or the Secretary of State or each of them (where each wishes to object) must, within a period specified by the court, file with the court and serve on the special advocate notice of any objection which the relevant person or the Secretary of State has to the proposed communication or to the form in which it is proposed to be made. [PART 82 – CLOSED MATERIAL PROCEDURE > 82.11] (6) Paragraph (2) does not prohibit the specially represented party from communicating with the special advocate after the relevant person has served material on the special advocate, but—

[PART 82 – CLOSED MATERIAL PROCEDURE > 82.11] (a) the specially represented party may only communicate with the special advocate in writing through the specially represented party’s legal representative; and

[PART 82 – CLOSED MATERIAL PROCEDURE > 82.11] (b) the special advocate must not reply to the communication other than in accordance with paragraph (3A) or directions of the court, except that the special advocate may without such directions send a written acknowledgment of receipt to the specially represented party’s legal representative. ## Evidence in proceedings to which this Part applies

## 82.12

[PART 82 – CLOSED MATERIAL PROCEDURE > 82.12] (1) Subject to the other rules in this Part, the evidence of a witness may be given either—

[PART 82 – CLOSED MATERIAL PROCEDURE > 82.12] (a) orally before the court; or

[PART 82 – CLOSED MATERIAL PROCEDURE > 82.12] (b) in writing, in which case it must be given in such manner and at such time as the court directs. [PART 82 – CLOSED MATERIAL PROCEDURE > 82.12] (2) The court may also receive evidence in documentary or any other form. [PART 82 – CLOSED MATERIAL PROCEDURE > 82.12] (3) The court may receive evidence that would not, but for this rule, be admissible in a court of law. [PART 82 – CLOSED MATERIAL PROCEDURE > 82.12] (4) Every party is entitled to adduce evidence and to cross-examine witnesses during any hearing or part of a hearing from which that party and that party’s legal representatives are not excluded. [PART 82 – CLOSED MATERIAL PROCEDURE > 82.12] (5) A special advocate is entitled to adduce evidence and to cross-examine a witness only during a hearing or part of a hearing from which the specially represented party and the specially represented party’s legal representatives are excluded. [PART 82 – CLOSED MATERIAL PROCEDURE > 82.12] (6) The court may require a witness to give evidence on oath. ## Sensitive material

## 82.13

[PART 82 – CLOSED MATERIAL PROCEDURE > 82.13] (1) The relevant person—

[PART 82 – CLOSED MATERIAL PROCEDURE > 82.13] (a) must apply to the court for permission to withhold sensitive material from a specially represented party or the specially represented party’s legal representative in accordance with this rule; and

[PART 82 – CLOSED MATERIAL PROCEDURE > 82.13] (b) may not rely on sensitive material at a hearing on notice unless a special advocate has been appointed to represent the interests of the specially represented party. [PART 82 – CLOSED MATERIAL PROCEDURE > 82.13] (2) The relevant person must file with the court and, at such time as the court directs, serve on the special advocate—

[PART 82 – CLOSED MATERIAL PROCEDURE > 82.13] (a) the sensitive material; and

[PART 82 – CLOSED MATERIAL PROCEDURE > 82.13] (b) a statement of the relevant person’s reasons for withholding that material from the specially represented party and the specially represented party’s legal representatives. [PART 82 – CLOSED MATERIAL PROCEDURE > 82.13] (3) The relevant person may at any time amend or supplement material filed under this rule, but only with—

[PART 82 – CLOSED MATERIAL PROCEDURE > 82.13] (a) the agreement of the special advocate; or

[PART 82 – CLOSED MATERIAL PROCEDURE > 82.13] (b) the permission of the court. ## Consideration of closed material application or of objection to special advocate’s communication

## 82.14

[PART 82 – CLOSED MATERIAL PROCEDURE > 82.14] (1) This rule applies where the relevant person or, as the case may be, the Secretary of State has—

[PART 82 – CLOSED MATERIAL PROCEDURE > 82.14] (a) applied under rule 82.13 (sensitive material) for permission to withhold sensitive material; or

[PART 82 – CLOSED MATERIAL PROCEDURE > 82.14] (b) objected under rule 82.11(5)(b) (special advocate: communicating about proceedings) to a proposed communication by the special advocate or to the form in which it is proposed to be made. [PART 82 – CLOSED MATERIAL PROCEDURE > 82.14] (2) The court must fix a hearing for the relevant party, the Secretary of State and the special advocate to make oral representations, unless—

[PART 82 – CLOSED MATERIAL PROCEDURE > 82.14] (a) the special advocate gives notice that he or she does not challenge the application or objection;

[PART 82 – CLOSED MATERIAL PROCEDURE > 82.14] (b) the court has previously, in determining the application under section 6(2) of the Act for a declaration, found that the first condition in section 6 of the Act is met in relation to the same or substantially the same material and is satisfied that it would be just to give permission without a hearing;

[PART 82 – CLOSED MATERIAL PROCEDURE > 82.14] (c) the court has previously considered—

[PART 82 – CLOSED MATERIAL PROCEDURE > 82.14] (i) an application under rule 82.13(1) for permission to withhold the same or substantially the same material; or

[PART 82 – CLOSED MATERIAL PROCEDURE > 82.14] (ii) an objection under rule 82.11(5)(b) to the same or substantially the same proposed communication; and is satisfied that it would be just to give permission or uphold the objection without a hearing; or

[PART 82 – CLOSED MATERIAL PROCEDURE > 82.14] (d) the relevant person, the Secretary of State and the special advocate consent to the court deciding the application or objection without a hearing. [PART 82 – CLOSED MATERIAL PROCEDURE > 82.14] (3) If the special advocate does not challenge the application or the objection, he or she must give notice of that fact to the court, the relevant person and the Secretary of State no later than the end of—

[PART 82 – CLOSED MATERIAL PROCEDURE > 82.14] (a) 14 days after the date on which the relevant person or the Secretary of State serves on the special advocate the notice under rule 82.11(5)(b) or the material under rule 82.13(2), or

[PART 82 – CLOSED MATERIAL PROCEDURE > 82.14] (b) such other period as the court may direct. [PART 82 – CLOSED MATERIAL PROCEDURE > 82.14] (4) Where the court fixes a hearing under this rule, the relevant person, the Secretary of State and the special advocate must before the hearing file with the court a schedule identifying the issues which cannot be agreed between them, which must also—

[PART 82 – CLOSED MATERIAL PROCEDURE > 82.14] (a) give brief reasons for their contentions in relation to each issue; and

[PART 82 – CLOSED MATERIAL PROCEDURE > 82.14] (b) set out any proposals for the court to resolve those issues. [PART 82 – CLOSED MATERIAL PROCEDURE > 82.14] (5) A hearing under this rule shall take place in the absence of the specially represented party and the specially represented party’s legal representative. [PART 82 – CLOSED MATERIAL PROCEDURE > 82.14] (6) Where the court has, in determining an application under section 6(2) of the Act for a declaration, found that the first condition in section 6 of the Act is met in relation to any material, it may give permission to withhold that material without a hearing in relation to that material, whether or not a hearing is required in relation to any other material. [PART 82 – CLOSED MATERIAL PROCEDURE > 82.14] (7) Where the court gives permission to the relevant person to withhold sensitive material, the court—

[PART 82 – CLOSED MATERIAL PROCEDURE > 82.14] (a) must consider whether to direct the relevant person to serve a summary of that material on the specially represented party and the specially represented party’s legal representative; but

[PART 82 – CLOSED MATERIAL PROCEDURE > 82.14] (b) must ensure that any such summary does not contain material the disclosure of which would be damaging to the interests of national security. [PART 82 – CLOSED MATERIAL PROCEDURE > 82.14] (8) If the court is satisfied that—

[PART 82 – CLOSED MATERIAL PROCEDURE > 82.14] (a) the relevant person does not intend to rely on sensitive material, and

[PART 82 – CLOSED MATERIAL PROCEDURE > 82.14] (b) that material does not adversely affect the relevant person’s case or support the case of another party to the proceedings, the court may direct that the relevant person must not rely in the proceedings on that material, without the court first requiring the relevant person to serve a summary of that material on the specially represented party and the specially represented party’s legal representative. [PART 82 – CLOSED MATERIAL PROCEDURE > 82.14] (9) Where the court has not given permission to the relevant person to withhold sensitive material from, or has directed the relevant person to serve a summary of that material on, the specially represented party and the specially represented party’s legal representative—

[PART 82 – CLOSED MATERIAL PROCEDURE > 82.14] (a) the relevant person shall not be required to serve that material or summary; but

[PART 82 – CLOSED MATERIAL PROCEDURE > 82.14] (b) if the relevant person does not do so, at a hearing on notice the court may—

[PART 82 – CLOSED MATERIAL PROCEDURE > 82.14] (i) if it considers that the material or anything that is required to be summarised might adversely affect the relevant person’s case or support the case of another party to the proceedings, direct that the relevant person is not to rely on such points in the relevant person’s case, or that the relevant person makes such concessions or takes such other steps as the court may direct; and

[PART 82 – CLOSED MATERIAL PROCEDURE > 82.14] (ii) in any other case, direct that the relevant person must not rely in the proceedings on that material or (as the case may be) on what is required to be summarised. [PART 82 – CLOSED MATERIAL PROCEDURE > 82.14] (10) The court must give permission to the relevant person to withhold sensitive material where it considers that disclosure of that material would be damaging to the interests of national security. ## Failure to comply with directions

## 82.15

[PART 82 – CLOSED MATERIAL PROCEDURE > 82.15] (1) Where a party or the special advocate fails to comply with a direction of the court, the court may serve on that person a notice which states—

[PART 82 – CLOSED MATERIAL PROCEDURE > 82.15] (a) the respect in which that person has failed to comply with the direction;

[PART 82 – CLOSED MATERIAL PROCEDURE > 82.15] (b) a time limit for complying with the direction; and

[PART 82 – CLOSED MATERIAL PROCEDURE > 82.15] (c) that the court may proceed to determine the proceedings before it on the material before it if that person fails to comply with the direction within that time limit. [PART 82 – CLOSED MATERIAL PROCEDURE > 82.15] (2) Where a party or the special advocate fails to comply with the direction after such a notice, the court may proceed in accordance with paragraph (1)(c). ## Judgments

## 82.16

[PART 82 – CLOSED MATERIAL PROCEDURE > 82.16] (1) Where the court gives judgment in any proceedings to which this Section applies, it may withhold any, or any part, of its reasons if and to the extent that it is not possible to give those reasons without disclosing information the disclosure of which would be damaging to the interests of national security. [PART 82 – CLOSED MATERIAL PROCEDURE > 82.16] (2) Where the judgment of the court does not include the full reasons for its decision, the court must serve on the relevant person, the Secretary of State (where not the relevant person) and the special advocate a separate written judgment giving those reasons. ## Application by the Secretary of State or relevant person for reconsideration of decision

## 82.17

[PART 82 – CLOSED MATERIAL PROCEDURE > 82.17] (1) If the court proposes, in any proceedings to which this Section applies, to serve on a specially represented party—

[PART 82 – CLOSED MATERIAL PROCEDURE > 82.17] (a) notice of any order or direction made or given in the absence of the Secretary of State or, if the relevant person is not the Secretary of State, the absence of the relevant person; or

[PART 82 – CLOSED MATERIAL PROCEDURE > 82.17] (b) any written judgment;

[PART 82 – CLOSED MATERIAL PROCEDURE > 82.17] then before the court serves any such notice or judgment on the specially represented party, it must first serve notice on the Secretary of State and, if the relevant person is not the Secretary of State, on the relevant person, of its intention to do so. [PART 82 – CLOSED MATERIAL PROCEDURE > 82.17] (2) The Secretary of State or relevant person may, within 5 days of being served with notice under paragraph (1), apply to the court to reconsider the terms of the order or direction or to review the terms of the proposed judgment if the Secretary of State or relevant person considers that—

[PART 82 – CLOSED MATERIAL PROCEDURE > 82.17] (a) the Secretary of State or relevant person’s compliance with the order or direction; or

[PART 82 – CLOSED MATERIAL PROCEDURE > 82.17] (b) the notification to the specially represented party of any matter contained in the judgment, order or direction, would cause information to be disclosed where such disclosure would be damaging to the interests of national security. [PART 82 – CLOSED MATERIAL PROCEDURE > 82.17] (3) Where the Secretary of State or relevant person makes an application under paragraph (2), the Secretary of State or relevant person must at the same time serve on the special advocate—

[PART 82 – CLOSED MATERIAL PROCEDURE > 82.17] (a) a copy of the application; and

[PART 82 – CLOSED MATERIAL PROCEDURE > 82.17] (b) a copy of the notice served on the Secretary of State or relevant person pursuant to paragraph (1). [PART 82 – CLOSED MATERIAL PROCEDURE > 82.17] (4) Rule 82.14 (consideration of closed material application or of objection to special advocate’s communication), except for paragraphs (6) to (8) of that rule, applies with any necessary modifications to the consideration of an application under paragraph (2) of this rule. [PART 82 – CLOSED MATERIAL PROCEDURE > 82.20] (1) This rule applies where the Secretary of State is not a party to relevant civil proceedings but—

[PART 82 – CLOSED MATERIAL PROCEDURE > 82.20] (a) it appears to—
